title: Publishing Truscott photo was 'heartless'
article: A letter from Peter Splinter, President of Braebury Homes Corporation in Kingston.

I am writing in response to the disturbing front-page photo in the Aug. 10 Whig-Standard. The picture shows the late Samuel Truscott in distress after an altercation with police in May 1997 and it doesn't represent a true picture of the events that occurred on Sunday, Aug. 8, 2004.

Mr. Truscott had been an employee of mine for 21/2 years. He worked as a construction labourer for Braebury Homes. I worked side by side with him on many occasions. Sam was a dedicated employee who always arrived on site at 6:30 a.m., prior to our 7 a.m. start time. He was a hard worker. He hadn't missed a day of work since May 2002. If he was asked to stay late to finish a task, he always made himself available.

My heart goes out to Mr. Truscott's family over the tragedy that occurred on Sunday morning. I'm shocked that while his family and friends were grieving, The Whig published a seven-year-old photo of him. His family is owed an apology.

According to The Whig's story, Sam walked into the hospital and advised medical staff that he had taken cocaine. Two-and-a-half hours later, while in hospital, he died. The picture The Whig printed certainly misled the public.

Would the individuals who chose to print the photo have published such a disturbing picture if Sam had been one of their family members? I think not. I'm sure that no one involved in the events that transpired on Sunday, from the individual who called police to the officers who responded to his home to the health-care workers at the hospital, is pleased about Mr.
Truscott's death. He made a poor decision and now his family and friends are living with the consequences.

The Whig's decision to print the seven-year-old picture of Sam was irresponsible, insensitive and heartless. We are all part of humanity and everyone deserves to be treated humanely. I, along with the hundreds of co-workers who worked with Sam, will miss him. We extend to his family our deepest sympathy.
